extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/prosecuting attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and eligibility criteria for requesting or imposing deferral/suspension of examination under 37 CFR 1.103, plus related rules on periods for reply, abandonment, and extensions under 37 CFR 1.135 and 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in a request for deferral of examination (37 CFR 1.103(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for deferral of examination under 37 CFR 1.103(d) must include: (A) a period of suspension, in a whole number of months, not extending beyond three years from the earliest effective filing date (if no period or an excessive period is submitted, the Office will assume the maximum period is requested); (B) the publication fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.18(d); and (C) the processing fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(i). Form PTO/SB/37 may be used to submit the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request includes no suspension period or one exceeding 3 years, the Office assumes the maximum is requested. The publication and processing fees required by the cited regulations must accompany the request when filed. Form PTO/SB/37 includes required fields, notice that deferral may reduce patent term adjustment, and signature/fee handling instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility conditions for granting deferral of examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will not grant a deferral of examination unless all of the following conditions are met: (A) the application is (1) an original utility or plant application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) or (2) an application resulting from entry of the international application into the national stage after compliance with 37 CFR 1.495 (the application cannot be a design application, a reissue application, or a CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d)); (B) the application was filed on or after November 29, 2000; (C) the applicant has not filed a nonpublication request under 37 CFR 1.213(a), or if one was filed the applicant must file a request under 37 CFR 1.213(b) to rescind it; (D) the application is in condition for publication as provided in 37 CFR 1.211(c); and (E) the Office has not issued either an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each element (A)-(E) is mandatory for grant. Example examiner reasons for denial include: applicant did not rescind a nonpublication request, a first Office action has been issued, or applicant has not requested voluntary publication under 37 CFR 1.221.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and form paragraphs for denying an improper deferral request
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request is improper, use the form paragraph ¶7.56.02 (Request for Deferral of Examination under 37 CFR 1.103(d), Denied) to notify the applicant of denial and insert the filing date and reason(s) for denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note examples: insert the filing date of the request and reasons such as failure to rescind a nonpublication request, issuance of a first Office action, or failure to submit a request for voluntary publication. See MPEP § 709 for cross-reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant of deferral requires supervisory approval and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: A supervisory patent examiner’s approval is required to grant a deferral of examination. Use the form paragraph ¶7.54.01 to notify applicant that the request has been approved and state the period of deferral in months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the notification insert the filing date of the request and the number of months for the deferral. Once granted, examination is suspended for the stated period and the application will not be taken up until the suspension expires (unless terminated earlier).

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of suspension of action at applicant's request
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may submit a request for termination of a suspension of action prior to the end of the suspension period. The request is effective when an appropriate official of the Office acts on it; if the suspension period has not expired when the Office acts, the Office will terminate the suspension and place the application on the examiner’s docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send acknowledgment to applicant using form paragraph ¶7.54.02 (Request for Termination of a Suspension of Action, Granted) and insert the filing date of the termination request. Termination should be acted upon immediately when the reason for suspension no longer exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office-initiated suspension limits and procedures (37 CFR 1.103(e)/(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension of action initiated by the Office should be avoided if possible and is limited to a maximum period of 6 months per suspension. An examiner may grant an initial Office-initiated suspension for up to 6 months; any second or subsequent suspension requires TC Director approval and must be signed by the TC Director. Suspensions under 37 CFR 1.103(f) are decided by the TC Director of work group 3640.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A notification of suspension must be mailed to applicant for each Office-initiated suspension and must include the suspension period. When the suspension period expires the examiner should take up action on the application or evaluate possibilities for giving an action on the merits (e.g., find another reference). If a second/subsequent suspension is necessary, obtain TC Director approval (see MPEP § 1003) and prepare another suspension notification signed by the TC Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs for Office-initiated suspensions (examples ¶7.52 and ¶7.53)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use designated form paragraphs when suspending prosecution awaiting a new reference (¶7.52) or for possible interference (¶7.53). Each such paragraph must state the suspension period in months and advise applicant to inquire as to the application's status upon expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes for these paragraphs reiterate the maximum suspension period of six months and TC Director approval/signature requirements for additional suspensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements and warnings in Form PTO/SB/37
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/37 (Request for Deferral of Examination) contains statements that deferral is suspension of action (may reduce patent term adjustment), requires the fees (processing and publication) when filed, provides for rescission of nonpublication under 37 CFR 1.213(b) if applicable, and includes signature, fee payment, and privacy/FOIA notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form includes a warning that information may become public and that credit card information should not be included on the form (use PTO-2038). It states that the publication fee and processing fee are required when the request is filed and that applications will be scheduled for publication at 18 months from earliest claimed filing date if nonpublication is rescinded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory period for reply and abandonment (35 U.S.C. 133; 37 CFR 1.135)
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum statutory period for reply to an Office action is six months (35 U.S.C. 133). Under 37 CFR 1.135(a) failure to reply within the time period provided under §1.134 and §1.136 will result in abandonment unless an Office action indicates otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.135(b) specifies that admission or refusal to admit amendments after final rejection or non-responsive amendments will not save the application from abandonment. See MPEP § 710.01 and related sections for treatment of replies and abandonment consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of bona fide replies with inadvertent omissions (37 CFR 1.135(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reply is a bona fide attempt to advance the application but inadvertently omits something, the examiner may accept it as adequate to avoid abandonment and give a shortened statutory period (generally 1 month) to supply the omission if the omission precludes action on the merits. If the omission does not preclude action on the merits, the examiner may waive the deficiency and act on the application or repeat/make final the rejection/objected matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of omissions that preclude action on the merits: unsigned amendment, improperly signed, or submission of additional claims requiring additional fees. The decision to provide a 1-month shortened statutory period is at the examiner's discretion and extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a)/(b) may be available unless the action indicates otherwise. If the omission was not inadvertent (abuse to gain time), do not grant the shortened period and notify applicant accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: How statutory reply periods are computed
rubrics_metrics.description: The time for reply is computed from the date stamped or printed on the Office action to the Office's date of receipt of the applicant’s reply. No cognizance is taken of fractions of a day. The reply is due on the corresponding calendar day of the month (e.g., 6 months after the Office action date), with special handling for end-of-month dates and leap years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: an action dated November 30 with a 3‑month period is due the following February 28 (or 29). A 1‑month extension shifts the due date to the corresponding day in the next month. A 30‑day period includes weekends and federal holidays but if a period ends on a weekend/holiday, filing on the next business day is timely. The date of receipt is the Office date stamp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136: general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.136(a)(1) an applicant required to reply within a nonstatutory or shortened statutory time period may extend the time up to the earlier of the expiration of any maximum statutory period or five months after the time set for reply by filing a petition and paying the fee, unless exceptions apply (e.g., notified otherwise in an Office action, certain appeal or hearing replies, contested cases). Paragraph (b) provides that when paragraph (a) is not available, extensions will be granted only for sufficient cause for a reasonable time and must be filed on or before the day the reply is due, accompanied by the petition fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date of filing the petition/fee is used to determine the extension period and fee amount. Certain replies (e.g., reply briefs under §41.41, requests for oral hearing under §41.47(a), replies in contested cases) are excepted from (a). Petitions under (b) must be accompanied by the §1.17(g) petition fee. See cross-references (§1.304, §1.550(c), §1.956, §§41.4(a)/41.121(a)(3)) for extensions in specific proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory periods: typical durations and situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Shortened statutory periods (not less than 30 days) are used in many cases. Some specific situations and typical shortened periods are: 1 month (not less than 30 days) for submitting an oath/declaration under §1.63 or formal drawings under §1.85(c) or certain deposits under §1.809(c); 2 months for specified matters such as reply by winning party in a terminated interference to an unanswered Office action or Ex parte Quayle (formal matters when application is otherwise in condition for allowance); 3 months to reply to any Office action on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An indication of a shortened time for reply should appear prominently on the first page of actions. Shortened periods are subject to the provisions of 37 CFR 1.136(a) unless the Office action notifies otherwise. Time limit actions (special specified times) may be used for consequences other than abandonment and should be typed in capital letters where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified time limits (time limit actions) — use and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain situations require the examiner to set a specified time for applicant to take some action where failure to timely act results in a consequence other than abandonment. These are called time limit actions and are established under authority of 35 U.S.C. 2 and 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time limit requirements should be indicated conspicuously (capital letters when required). Examples and detailed situations are set out in subsequent MPEP sections; the excerpt notes that time limits are distinct from shortened statutory periods and produce different consequences.
